The Difference Between Pure Water and Tap Water for Car Washing | Why White Water Spot Marks Remain

"I rinsed it thoroughly, but white rings remained on the dry body." One cause of this is the minerals dissolved in tap water. "Pure water," which you may see on car wash menus, is water from which these minerals have been almost entirely removed. Using it for the final rinse makes it less likely that water-derived marks will be left behind.
Hello. This is Macchan, the car washer from Higashiomi, at Green Road SS (Yokaichi Gas Co., Ltd.) in Higashiomi City, Shiga Prefecture.
Why do white rings remain after water droplets disappear?
A photo showing whitish stains on the door mirror and side panel. The header image is the same car. From a photo taken before Mineral Off treatment on our shop blog (posted October 18, 2026).

For example, suppose a single water droplet remains on the hood after washing. As time passes, the moisture evaporates, but components like calcium that were dissolved in the water remain there. That is why you see white rings along the places where the water droplets were.

However, not everything that looks white on the body is necessarily a tap water mark. The photo is of a car we previously introduced as an example of Mineral Off treatment at our shop.
